title: Closure Rate of Primary Macular Foramina: ILM Peeling vs ILM Flap
summary:
Primary macular foramen is a rare condition affecting the vitreoretinal interface,
but it is regularly diagnosed and
treated surgically at specialized ophthalmology centers. If left untreated, it can lead to progressive vision loss with
significant impairment of central visual acuity; therefore, surgical intervention is typically indicated for symptomatic
macular foramina are generally indicated for surgical treatment. For
surgical therapy, various surgical techniques are available, the
choice of which depends, among other things, on patient-specific factors, the size of the lesion, and the
surgeon’s preference.

conditions: Degeneration of macula and posterior pole

interventions.name:
The study includes patients with primary macular foramen who
underwent surgical treatment at Frankfurt University Hospital via pars plana vitrectomy using either the ILM peeling or ILM flap technique. A prerequisite for

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data sets are included if the following criteria are met:
- A clinically confirmed diagnosis followed by surgical
treatment, as documented in the medical assessment in the patient’s medical record.
- Fully documented preoperative and postoperative clinical findings,
including OCT imaging and visual acuity measurements
- A sufficient follow-up period to assess the
anatomical closure of the macular hole
- All procedures performed by the same vitreoretinal surgeon
- Complete baseline data (age, sex, diagnosis, date of examination).
Exclusion criteria:
- Secondary macular foramina (e.g., traumatic or otherwise associated)
- Unclear or missing reference diagnosis in the patient’s medical record,
- Incomplete clinical documentation
